references.text: In Matthew's parallel account of the crucifixion, Simon of Cyrene is also mentioned as being forced to carry Jesus' cross ([ref:Matt 27:32|Matthew 27:32]).
Mark's parallel account identifies Simon of Cyrene as the father of Alexander and Rufus, and states that he was forced to carry the cross ([ref:Mark 15:21|Mark 15:21]).

John tells us that Jesus himself carried his cross out to Golgotha. Together with Luke's account, this gives a complete picture: Jesus carried the cross himself at first, but Simon took over along the way ([ref:Joh 19:17|John 19:17]).

Jesus said that whoever wants to follow him must take up their cross daily and follow him. Simon of Cyrene became a literal picture of this discipleship by carrying the cross behind Jesus ([ref:Luk 9:23|Luke 9:23]).
Jesus' words about taking up one's cross and following him find a concrete fulfillment in Simon of Cyrene, who carried the cross "behind Jesus" ([ref:Luk 14:27|Luke 14:27]).
Paul greets Rufus and his mother in Rome. Rufus may be the son of Simon of Cyrene mentioned by Mark, showing that Simon's family became part of the early church ([ref:Rom 16:13|Romans 16:13]).

The prophecy about the Lord's suffering servant who bears our burdens. That Simon had to help Jesus carry the cross shows the physical exhaustion Jesus endured, in line with Isaiah's prophecy ([ref:Jes 53:4|Isaiah 53:4]).
